symptom: Confirming a Nomi-generated storyboard design could bypass the durable production artifact review and materialization path because the creation UI could not prove which candidate artifact contained the selected local plan.
direct_cause: The production driver calculated and persisted planHash in storyboard-vN.json but omitted that same value from the candidate artifact contentHash field consumed by the renderer.
class_root: Storyboard content identity was written to the file-backed plan and the run artifact as two separate contracts, allowing the durable orchestration record to lose the only safe join key used by the multi-design creation UI.
affected_population: Users confirming a storyboard produced by an active production run after selecting among multiple local storyboard designs
Users reopening an older production run whose candidate storyboard artifact predates contentHash persistence
entry_points: production.plan-storyboard candidate creation after an approved script
production run read used by the creation workspace before storyboard review and materialization
internal_only_reason: The defect is entirely within Nomi's own production artifact persistence and renderer join contract. No provider, model, or third-party API behavior determines the invariant.
invariants: Every newly proposed storyboard artifact carries the SHA-256 of the exact JSON plan stored in its file-backed record as both planHash and artifact contentHash.
A legacy storyboard candidate without contentHash is enriched only when its project-owned regular file has a valid 64-character planHash that exactly matches a fresh SHA-256 of its plan object.
Missing, malformed, symlinked, out-of-project, or hash-mismatched storyboard files remain unbound and cannot be guessed from candidate order.
migration: No persisted schema version changes. New candidates persist contentHash directly. Existing candidates remain byte-for-byte unchanged; the read path derives a verified in-memory contentHash from their protected storyboard-vN.json record when possible, so they can use the same review and materialization flow without rewriting history.
residual_risks: Legacy storyboard files that are missing or already corrupted cannot be safely rebound and require the user to regenerate the candidate.
Content hashes identify exact JSON serialization; intentionally reformatted historical plan files fail closed instead of being semantically canonicalized.
